clue.text: Show of French films, 50% censored

parts.note: de is the French word for of

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away, so only its first half survives the censor

parts.note: pictures is an everyday word for films

explanation.surface: A French film season has half its content cut by the censors.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% censored' cuts the last four letters from PICTURES, leaving PICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something in a picture or in words is to show it.

clue.text: Played in charge of teacher

parts.note: did act is a way of saying played a part

explanation.surface: Someone acted as the person in charge of a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' gives DID ACT, two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to instruct, the manner of a schoolmaster.

clue.text: Tripe ends up doing for such as Bush

indicators.note: up here means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Rubbish ends up being the undoing of George Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' (as in stirred up) rearranges TRIPE ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bush, father and son, both held the highest office in the United States.

clue.text: Ready partner of 8

explanation.surface: Ready money and a singer's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny Cash married and sang with June Carter, the answer to 8 down. 'Ready' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is notes and coins, and Johnny Cash was the singing husband of June Carter.

clue.text: Mountain range thus surrounding Spielberg's park

annotationWithheld.why: Mountain range thus surrounding Spielberg's park (8): JURA (mountain range) + SIC (thus) gives only seven letters; no clue word supplies the second S, and 'surrounding' has nothing to put inside
annotationWithheld.clue: Mountain range thus surrounding Spielberg's park

clue.text: Oddly ugly rioter somehow hidden

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the word ugly
somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: An ugly rioter with some concealed motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' gives U and L; 'somehow' rearranges RIOTER to TERIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is one kept concealed beneath the stated reason.

clue.text: Weapon with a firm mounted casing for large animals

parts.note: arm is short for firearm, a weapon

indicators.note: the word solid forms a case round the letter for large
in a down clue mounted means climbing, so the piece is read upwards

parts.note: firm and solid are synonyms

explanation.surface: An armed security firm guards a big beast with a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casing for' puts L in SOLID; 'mounted' turns SOLLID upwards to DILLOS. Armadillos are themselves armoured, so 'casing' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Armadillos are burrowing mammals of the Americas with bony armour.

clue.text: Prevents acne possibly escalating

indicators.note: in a down clue escalating means rising, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: spots are what acne may produce

explanation.surface: Something that stops acne getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escalating' turns SPOTS upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or block something is to keep it from happening.

clue.text: One transporting partner of 3

explanation.surface: A delivery driver and a singer's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: June Carter married and sang with Johnny Cash, the answer to 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver of goods carts is a haulier, and June Carter was the wife of Johnny Cash.

clue.text: Tarzan's woman has time for another

parts.note: Jane is Tarzan's companion in the stories

explanation.surface: Tarzan's partner makes time for another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another woman, after Tarzan's Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet is another female name, a second woman after Tarzan's.

clue.text: Make intermittent haste over lantern fish's habitat

indicators.note: in this clue over means turned over, so the whole run is read backwards
only every other letter of the word make is taken, in stop-start fashion

parts.note: speed is a synonym of haste

explanation.surface: An instruction to hurry in fits and starts over a lantern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittent' takes A and E from MAKE; with SPEED that is AESPEED, and 'over' turns the whole run back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantern fish live far below the surface in the ocean depths.

clue.text: Rumba to beaten drum

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dancers do the rumba to the beat of a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' rearranges the letters of RUMBA and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a kind of drum, especially a small one used in older music.

clue.text: Feature covered by some yogic Hindus

indicators.note: the answer lies covered inside some of the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A facial feature covered by the beards of some yogic Hindus.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Feature covered' as the definition, but 'covered by some' is the hidden-word indicator, so the definition is 'Feature' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the face below the mouth is one of its features.

clue.text: Sappers standing by oil that is finally due to break out again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
crude is unrefined oil
sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is or namely

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word due

explanation.surface: Army engineers stand guard by an oil supply that is about to erupt again.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the abbreviation of scilicet, 'that is'. 'finally' gives E, the last letter of 'due'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recrudescence is the renewed outbreak of a disease or trouble after a lull.

clue.text: Point old Ford somewhere south of the Wash

parts.note: east is a compass point
the Anglia was a Ford car made from 1939 to 1967

explanation.surface: A vintage Ford parked somewhere in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a bay on England's east coast; East Anglia, the region of Norfolk and Suffolk, lies south of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of Norfolk and Suffolk lies just below the bay on England's east coast.

clue.text: Zap bruise initially with a good cold compress

parts.note: to zap and to ice are both slang for kill

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word bruise is taken

explanation.surface: Treating a bruise quickly with a good cold compress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zap' is US slang for kill, as is ICE. 'initially' gives B, the first letter of 'bruise'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag filled with ice is held on an injury to reduce swelling.

clue.text: Fish, perch, decaudated by canal gate

indicators.note: decaudated means having its tail cut off, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: a perch or pole was an old measure of length
a lock is the gated chamber that lets boats change level on a canal

explanation.surface: A perch with its tail removed lies beside a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' and 'perch' both look like fish, but perch here is POLE, an old unit of length; 'decaudated' (tail-cut) drops its E.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a food fish of the cod family found in North Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Sainted cleric sadly dies

parts.note: a canon is a cleric attached to a cathedral

indicators.note: sadly here means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A holy churchman dies, to everyone's sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges DIES to ISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone declared a saint by the church is sainted.

clue.text: Cheat starts to copy throughout exam relating to higher qualification

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A student cheats by copying all through an exam for a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheat' looks like the doctor-as-falsify verb but is DO; 'starts to' gives C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest academic degree, so this adjective concerns it.

clue.text: State of nation and people

parts.note: the words nation and people mean the same thing, and the clue asks for the condition they share

explanation.surface: A survey of how a country and its citizens are faring.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words with equal meanings are in a relation of sameness of sense.

clue.text: Such as Victoria's position

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria's place in society.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a London rail terminus, and one's post or rank in life is one's station.

clue.text: Reckon gentry ultimately will form such a set?

parts.note: to count is to reckon up a number

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word gentry

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the landed gentry make up a particular social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'county set' is a British term for the landed gentry of the shires, which ties the definition to 'gentry'.
explanation.definitionFit: The county set is the upper-class landowning circle of rural England.

clue.text: Judge wag is weaving this puzzle

indicators.note: weaving suggests the letters are interlaced into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A judge and a joker are working on a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' rearranges WAG IS to IGSAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces to reassemble is a puzzle.

clue.text: Worthless object's half wasted talent

indicators.note: the first half of the phrase is thrown away, leaving the other

parts.note: a trinket or ornament of little value, written as a hyphenated rhyming pair of words

explanation.surface: Half of a worthless trinket's talent has been wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half wasted' throws away the first half of KNICK-KNACK, keeping the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A knack is a skill or flair for doing something.

clue.text: Shameless confessor's claim

explanation.surface: Someone at confession says one thing while feeling no shame at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PENITENT, the answer is what a confessor claims, while as one word it means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Without remorse means unrepentant, while a person confessing would say they are sorry for their sins.

clue.text: In whist, play safe

explanation.surface: A cautious move at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: To peter in whist or bridge is to play a high card then a low one as a signal; peter is also old criminal slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing high then low signals a partner in whist, and a strongbox was called this by safe-crackers.

clue.text: Keen on binding books I love

indicators.note: the outer letters bind round the books, holding them inside

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A bookbinder's passion for the craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' puts NT inside I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To be into something is informally to be enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Well in pocket

explanation.surface: A well dug into a pocket of land.
explanation.walkthrough: A billiard table's pocket is this, as is a well sunk in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a shaft dug in the ground, and a snooker pocket is an opening in the table.

clue.text: He's arranged letters

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the word that follows are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A typesetter or signwriter who has put the letters in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges LETTERS; read whole, the clue also describes someone who has settled or fixed things.
explanation.definitionFit: One who settles matters is someone who arranges them, and the clue says this person has done so.

clue.text: Linguist primarily, critic having opposed Vietnam as rank folly ultimately

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of the three words that follow
ultimately means the last letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A critic who opposed the Vietnam War as utter folly.
explanation.walkthrough: Noam Chomsky, the American linguist, was a prominent opponent of the Vietnam War, so the surface describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Noam Chomsky is a celebrated American scholar of language and grammar.

clue.text: Practical Labour Business Secretary loses his head

parts.note: labour means work

indicators.note: his head is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: Vince Cable was the UK Business Secretary from 2010 to 2015

explanation.surface: A Labour plan is workable once the Business Secretary is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable was Britain's Business Secretary when the puzzle appeared; 'loses his head' drops the C. 'Labour' looks like the political party but means work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something feasible that can be made to function is practical.

clue.text: Day's delay potentially lethal

parts.note: D is a standard abbreviation for day

indicators.note: potentially suggests the letters could be reshaped into another word

explanation.surface: A day's delay could prove fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the usual abbreviation for day; 'potentially' rearranges the five letters of 'delay' to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal and deadly are synonyms describing something that kills.
